3

Week 10 matchups

Each game side by side: every offence against the defence it faces, special teams, and coaching tendencies. Pick a game, or use the cards at the bottom of this section.

How to read the expected values. "Expected in this matchup" adds the offence's and the defence's opponent-adjusted effects to the league average, plus home field. Each effect is first pulled towards the league average in proportion to how little data supports it (empirical-Bayes shrinkage), so a unit with few plays or noisy results moves the expectation very little. Confidence describes how much of each team's own record survives that shrinkage: moderate, low, very low, or no signal yet. Nothing here is a score or a result forecast, and no earlier season's results enter a team's own numbers. Early in a season such expectations have been too extreme, so each is also scaled by how well they held up at this week in 2021-25 (Method). Coaching labels describe what each staff has done in 2026 on small samples: 20-40 fourth-down decisions per team.

All week 10 games at a glance

The three largest unit-versus-unit edges in each game, scored on the shrunk matchup effects: each unit's effect times the share of it that survives shrinkage, in standard deviations, added for the two units (1.0 or more is notable: in 2021-25 an edge that size pointed the right way in 66% of 994 cases, against 53% for edges under 0.5). A measure with no reliable team-to-team signal cannot become a headline edge. Select a card to open the game.

4

Offence

EfficiencyDrivesPassingProtectionQuarterbacksPlayersRushingExplosives
EPA and DVOA are different measures. EPA (expected points added) values each play by the change in nflfastR's expected points from before to after the snap, from down, distance, field position and time. It is open, play-by-play and unadjusted unless an adjustment is applied. DVOA (FTN) compares each play's success with a league baseline for the same situation, then adjusts for opponent and removes some luck-driven outcomes. DVOA is proprietary, is not in nflverse and is not shown here. The opponent-adjusted columns are EPA and success rate adjusted by a published regression (Method), not DVOA.

Efficiency

Garbage time: how much of each offence's production came in lopsided game states. "Flatter it" means the raw yards, points and EPA look better than the team has played in competitive snaps; "understate it" means the reverse. Every rating in this report uses all snaps.

Drives and scoring

Per-drive rates remove differences in the number of possessions. Points over start EP measures what a unit did with the field position it was given.

Passing

Quarterback and protection are separated where the data allows: hit/sack versus clean-pocket EPA, sacks per pressure (partly the quarterback), drops and YAC over expected (receivers). Man and zone coverage splits are not available in free data.

Pass protection

Quarterbacks

Per quarterback, not per team: a team's totals can mix several passers. Composite = 50% opponent-adjusted EPA/dropback, 30% CPOE, 20% interception-worthy rate (lower is better). This weighting is a stated judgement, not a fitted model.

Quarterback situations: where team figures mix passers

Team passing figures elsewhere include every quarterback who played. This table splits them, so a returning starter or a backup can be judged on his own games. Status comes from the latest roster and injury report.

Offensive players: usage, game logs and rankings

Who gets the ball for each offence: targets, carries and their share of the team's, the last three games beside the season, and each player's status. A player now out who took a large share of the targets or carries matters more than his snap share suggests. Shares of the work settle quickly; per-target and per-carry efficiency is mostly noise over a few games (see Method).

Rushing

Designed runs, quarterback designed runs and scrambles are kept apart. Yards before contact points to blocking; yards after contact and rush yards over expected point to the ball carrier. Both are imperfect splits.

Efficiency and drives

Pass defence and coverage

Blitzing and pressure

Three different things. Blitz rate is how often a defence sends five or more rushers (FTN charting). Pressure rate is how often the quarterback is hurried, hit or sacked (PFR, game totals). Sack rate is sacks per dropback. A defence can blitz a lot without pressure, or create pressure with four and keep seven in coverage.

Individual pass rushers and coverage defenders

Who makes each defence's pressure and who gets targeted in coverage (PFR). A team whose pressure comes from one or two players loses much more when one of them is out than its team pressure rate suggests.

Special teams and coaching

CoachingSpecial teams

Coaching: who decides what

Each tendency is credited to the person who owns that decision. The head coach owns game management (fourth downs, two-point tries, end of half) even when he calls no plays; the play-callers own the play choices; the special-teams coordinator owns the units, with the head coach making the risky calls. These are observed decisions, not judgements of coaching quality.

The fourth-down reference compares each decision with historical average outcomes (2021-25), not with a win-probability model.

Turnovers, margin and sustainability

Expected values use FTN's interception-worthy charting and fumble counts. A large gap between actual and expected margin suggests regression is possible, not certain.

Luck, close games and regression candidates

Close-game records are not treated as luck on their own: quarterback quality, coaching and late-game execution all affect them. The categories are under Team profiles.

Penalties: offensive and defensive discipline

Counts are accepted penalties. Pre-snap fouls are the most clearly controllable. Pass interference, holding and illegal contact also come with aggressive coverage, and some calls are judgement calls by the officials.

Referee crews

Workload, possession and defensive fatigue

How much each offence leaves its defence on the field, and whether that has measurably hurt defences.

Rest, travel and body clock

Week 10 schedule context for every team, then the historical evidence (2002-25 regular seasons) behind it. Effects are measured as points beyond what each team's season strength predicts, using leave-one-game-out ratings.

Strength of schedule and quality of opposition

Opponent strength is the opponents' opponent-adjusted net EPA per play, not their records. Tiers are league thirds of that rating. Results against tiers rest on two or three games each.

Depth, injuries and personnel

Confirmed absences (reserve list, Out/Doubtful, or inactive for each of the last three games) are kept apart from Questionable and unexplained absences. Absences are weighted by snap share, not by an invented point value. A report for a game the player then played is not counted.

9

Data, validation and method

Window: 2026 regular season, weeks 1-9 (136 games, 17,507 scrimmage plays, 2,830 drives). Generated 2026-11-11T21:39:45+00:00. Historical seasons 2021-2025 are used only for reference models and weights, never as 2026 evidence.

Plays and filters

  • Scrimmage play: nflfastR pass or rush flag, EPA present, down present (two-point tries excluded), kneel-downs and spikes excluded. Plays nullified by penalty that nflfastR tags as a pass or rush are included, as in nflfastR's standard team summaries.
  • Dropback = pass attempts, sacks and scrambles. Designed rush = nflfastR rush (scrambles excluded). QB designed runs are designed rushes by players with 5+ dropbacks; they are reported separately from scrambles.
  • Success = EPA > 0. Early downs = 1st and 2nd. Late downs = third- and fourth-down conversion flags. Red zone = inside the opponent's 20.
  • Explosive: completed or attempted pass (not a scramble or sack) gaining 20+ yards; designed rush or scramble gaining 10+ yards; live plays only.
  • WP 10-90% columns drop plays when either side's win probability is outside 10-90%, as a garbage-time check.
  • Hit-or-sack rate uses the pbp qb_hit and sack flags. It is a proxy, not pressure: free data has no play-level pressure.

Opponent adjustment

For each metric (EPA/play, success, EPA/dropback, EPA/designed rush, early-down EPA) a play-level least-squares fit y = intercept + home + offence(team) + defence(team) with sum-to-zero team effects and no shrinkage. The adjusted value is the league mean plus the team effect, so a raw and an adjusted value sit on the same scale. Schedule strength is the play-weighted average opponent effect. The home coefficient this season is -0.010 EPA/play. Quarterback adjustment subtracts the average dropback-defence effect of the defences each passer faced.

Composite rankings and weights

EPA/play, success rate and points per drive measure overlapping things, so the composites are weighted by how well each one, measured over weeks 1-9, predicted a team's opponent-adjusted EPA/play over the rest of the season in 2021-2025 (non-negative least squares on within-season z-scores, 160 team-seasons). The regression handles their correlation, so nothing is double-counted.

adj. EPA/playadj. successpts/driveR² (combined)
Offence weights56%44%0%0.38
Offence single-metric R²0.350.330.29
Defence weights58%42%0%0.15
Defence single-metric R²0.140.120.11

Nine-week defensive numbers explain only about a tenth of rest-of-season defensive performance (R² 0.15), against about a third for offence (0.38). Read defensive rankings with more caution.

Overall team rating = (adj. offensive EPA/play − league mean) × 64.4 plays + (league mean − adj. defensive EPA/play) × 64.4 + special-teams EPA per game, in points per game. EPA is in points, so this needs no arbitrary weights. Special teams is kept separate everywhere else. Situational = equal-weight z-scores of late-down conversion and red-zone TD rate (two distinct situations). Passing, rushing, pass D, run D rank on one adjusted metric each.

Prior-season stabilisation

The "with 2025 prior" rating shrinks each 2026 adjusted EPA/play towards a prior of league mean + b × (team's 2025 adjusted value − 2025 mean). Year-to-year slopes from 2021-2025: offence b = 0.41, defence b = 0.20. The weight on 2026 is τ² / (τ² + σ²/n), with τ² the variance of true change between seasons (offence 0.0049, defence 0.0022) and σ²/n the sampling variance of this season's estimate. On average the 2026 data gets 59% of the weight on offence and 39% on defence, and the share rises each week. Teams with a new primary quarterback are flagged, because last season's offence then says less.

Scoring and drives

Drives are nflfastR fixed_drive. Points per drive are the offence's score change from the start of the drive to the start of the next drive, so extra points count and defensive or return scores do not. Every game's drive points reconcile to its final score. Points over start EP = drive points minus nflfastR's expected points at the first snap. That measures finishing relative to field position (it is a next-score expectation, so it is approximate).

Expected wins, luck and turnovers

  • Pythagorean expected wins use exponent 2.37.
  • EPA-based expected wins: P(win) = logistic(0.596 × game net EPA), fitted on 2021-2025 games, summed over games played.
  • Luck index = mean of (wins − Pythagorean xW) and (wins − EPA xW). At +0.75 or more a team is a potential overperformer, at −0.75 or less a potential underperformer. With 6-7 games the sampling error of either difference is about one win.
  • Expected interceptions: each charted attempt gets the league rate for its FTN interception-worthy status (worthy 58.6%, not worthy 0.36%). Expected fumbles lost: own fumbles × 0.486, the 2021-25 loss rate.

Fourth downs

A transparent reference, not nfl4th. For 4th downs with win probability 20-80% and more than two minutes left in the half, each option (go, punt, field goal) is valued at the average expected points after that choice in the same distance × field-position bucket in 2021-25 (buckets with 20+ cases). Selection bias (teams go when conditions favour it) and ignoring the clock limit it.

Penalties

nflfastR records one penalty per play, so no play is counted twice. Declined and offsetting penalties are excluded from the counts. Phase: special teams if the play was a kick, otherwise offence or defence by the penalised team. The EPA cost counts no-play penalties only; for accepted penalties on live plays the penalty and the play cannot be separated. Negated explosive plays and TDs are parsed from the play text.

Week 10 matchup expectations

For each measure in the matchup tables, the same additive fit as the opponent adjustment (offence + defence + home, sum-to-zero) is run on 2026 plays, drives or PFR team-games. Each team effect is then shrunk by w = τ² / (τ² + σ²/n), where σ²/n is its sampling variance and τ² the between-team variance of the effects minus their average sampling variance (method of moments). That weight proved too large early in a season. In a backtest on 2021-25 (1,916 team-games per measure), fitting on weeks 1 to W and predicting week W+1 for W = 4 to 16, the real gap from the league average was 37% of the expected gap at weeks 4-5 and 103% at weeks 14-16 (all measures pooled). Each weight is therefore multiplied by a factor for the week and the measure, fitted on those seasons and never above 1: after week 9 it is 0.80 for EPA per play, 0.72 for EPA per dropback, 0.62 for EPA per rush, 0.47 for pressure rate, 0.25 for turnovers per drive and 0.05 for red-zone TD rate, whose team effects did not predict the next game. Checked out of sample (each season from the other four), this lowered the error on 17 of 17 measures. Expected value = league mean + woff × offence effect + wdef × defence effect ± home effect. When τ² is close to zero, the measure has no reliable team-to-team signal yet and the expectation stays at the league average. This week that applies to: EPA per designed rush (defence). No earlier season's results enter a team's effects, and no score or result is forecast.

Matchup report rules

Eleven mismatch types are scanned in both directions for every game: rushing vs run defence, passing vs pass defence, strong protection vs weak rush, weak protection vs elite rush, mobile quarterback vs scramble containment, explosive passing vs deep-ball defence, four-man pressure vs protection, blitz rate vs passing against five-plus rushers, red zone, turnovers, and tackling vs yards after contact and catch. A finding needs one unit in roughly the top 8-10 and the other in the bottom 8-10 for that pairing. Each finding lists its evidence, the mechanism, what could neutralise it, and whether a more specific split supports it: run direction (inside vs outside), deep attempts, or the likely quarterback's own numbers. Confidence is strong only when both ranks are extreme and the shrinkage step keeps at least half of each team's record, moderate when it keeps at least a third, otherwise limited. Penalty vulnerabilities are hypotheses built from rates per opportunity (per 100 snaps or dropbacks) and fouls drawn by the opponent. Workload levels: plausible = a top-8 defensive snap count in the last game plus a short week; minor = one of those, or a top-8 three-and-out or quick-turnaround rate on a short week.

Workload and fatigue

Team snaps come from PFR snap counts (the most snaps any player on the unit played). Possession time, plays and three-and-outs come from nflfastR drives. Real rest is wall-clock time between the last play of one defensive drive and the first play of the next in the same half, so it includes kicks and stoppages. The fatigue study pools 2021-2026 play-by-play. It regresses EPA (and success) allowed on workload measures with defence-season and offence-season fixed effects (two-way demeaning), quarter and score-state controls, and game-clustered standard errors.

Weather line

Each outdoor game shows the National Weather Service forecast (Open-Meteo for other venues or if NWS cannot be read) for the kickoff hour and the next three hours: rain or snow is called likely at a 50%+ chance of precipitation in any of those hours, and wind is the mean over them. Early forecasts are rough, and a game whose forecast could not be re-read keeps the last one with its read time. Games with rain, snow or 15+ mph wind add what similar games did. Those are raw averages from 922 outdoor and open-roof 2021-25 regular-season games with a usable play-by-play weather text, not adjusted for teams; that text describes conditions around kickoff. Pass rate uses plays with win probability of 20-80%. Display only: no rating, edge or expected figure changes.

Rest, travel and body clock

Each team's home stadium sets its home time zone (zone rules applied on the game date, including the end of daylight saving time and Arizona's exception). Neutral-site international venues are mapped by stadium name. The historical study uses 2002-2025 regular-season games at home venues: each game's margin is compared with a leave-one-game-out season rating of both teams plus home field, and the away team's residual is averaged by time-zone direction (2+ zones east or west, one zone, same zone) and kickoff slot (early before 3pm ET, late, night from 7pm ET), and by kickoff time on the away team's home clock. Relocated franchises use their city at the time; a few home games played away from the usual stadium are not corrected.

Quarterback scenarios

Per-quarterback opponent-adjusted EPA per dropback is shrunk towards the league average, using his own dropbacks as the sample size, then combined with the opposing defence's effect. The spread between quarterbacks is fitted on 2021-2025: for each passer-season, his first 30, 60, 120 or 200 dropbacks were compared with the rest of his season (703 samples from 76 passers who went on to 150+ more dropbacks, so mostly starters). Only 19% of a quarterback's gap from average after 60 dropbacks, 28% after 120 and 34% after 200 carried forward, less than the team-level spread implied, so a short hot or cold run moves the expectation little. Capping big plays, success rate and dropping a passer's best quarter were tested and predicted no better beyond noise, so they are not used. When one quarter supplied more than half of a passer's total EPA and leaving it out moves his average by 0.10 or more per dropback, the quarterback line says so and gives his average without it, as a warning only. Status comes from each team's latest weekly roster (reserve list) and latest injury report (game status, or practice participation before game statuses are published). Team-level tables are not changed.

The same test for other positions (2021-2025, players who went on to 50+ more opportunities): after 40 carries about 11% of a running back's EPA-per-carry gap from average lasted (1074 samples), after 40 targets about 7% of a wide receiver's EPA-per-target gap (917 samples), after 20 targets about 17% for tight ends, and running backs' EPA per target showed no measurable carry-over. Success rate and capped EPA were no better. Early target share, by contrast, kept a correlation of about 0.47 with later target share. Player efficiency feeds no expectation in this report; the player tables and next-man-up lines show it with a 95% range and point to usage as the steadier guide.

Not available, and proxies used

  • Depth charts: ESPN's daily team depth charts via nflverse, used only for the next player listed behind an absent regular and for checking the listed QB and offensive line against who played the latest game (snap counts). Teams often leave charts stale, and a few chart rows carry stale player ids, which are repaired from the weekly rosters by team and name. Next Gen receiving: season rows for qualifying receivers, aggregated per team weighted by targets (separation, cushion, air yards) or catches (YAC over expected).
  • Individual pass rushers and coverage: PFR advanced defence, one row per defender per game, summed per player and team (a traded player appears under each team). "Per 100 snaps" uses all defensive snaps, not pass rushes, so it understates pass rushers on defences that face many runs. Coverage figures are for the nearest defender on targeted throws; passer rating allowed is recomputed from the summed targets, completions, yards, TDs and INTs. Status comes from the absences in section 16. FTN box counts, motion, RPO, no-huddle, contested targets and QB-fault sacks: FTN play charting, matched to play-by-play.
  • Offensive player usage, game logs and rankings: from the same play-by-play (rbsdm.com's box scores are built from it too). Targets are pass attempts with a receiver; carries are designed rushes (scrambles excluded; about 3% of designed rushes, mostly aborted snaps, have no ball carrier and are left out); shares are of the team's totals; "last 3" is the team's last three games. Position, name and status come from the weekly roster and the absences; snap share from snap counts; RYOE and separation from Next Gen weekly rows. Rankings need minimum volume and are season figures only.
  • Run direction, targets by position and throw zones: play-by-play run location (inside = middle or guard gap; outside = tackle or end), the targeted receiver's position on the weekly roster (fullbacks count as RBs), and nflfastR throw location (deep = 15+ air yards; left, middle, right). Run direction is not the blocking scheme, and position is not alignment: free data has neither run concepts nor slot vs outside receivers.
  • Win rates (pass block, pass rush, run block, run stop): ESPN Analytics, built from NFL Next Gen Stats tracking. They are not in nflverse, so they are copied by hand each week from ESPN's team table with its date (the win-rates file in the analytics scripts), shown for context only and not used in any rating, composite or matchup expectation. A pass block win means the line held its blocks for 2.5 seconds; a pass rush win means a rusher beat his block within 2.5 seconds.
  • DVOA: FTN's proprietary metric. It is not in nflverse and is not used or shown in this report. The closest computed analogues here are opponent-adjusted EPA and success rate. They are not DVOA.
  • Coverage (man/zone), time to pressure, pressure by play: not in free data. PFR pressures are game-level, so pressure-when-blitzing uses the hit-or-sack proxy.
  • Pressure coverage: PFR advanced stats are available for 122 of 136 games; pressure rates use only those games.
  • FTN charting is missing 2026_09_BUF_MIN, so blitz and expected-INT figures for those teams have fewer games.
  • Participation data (players on field per play) is not published for 2026, so personnel groupings and on/off splits are not possible. Availability uses snap counts, weekly rosters and injury reports.
  • Week 10 injury reports: 2 teams with a listed absence or practice concern already have a week 10 report. Other statuses come from each team's latest report and latest weekly roster; game statuses before the final report are practice participation only.
  • Timeout use is not scored: there is no defensible free benchmark. Bye effects rest on one game per team.
  • Blitz: FTN's blitz is five or more rushers, so "blitz" and "5+ rushers" are the same split here.

Small samples

Rates on very few cases are shown in muted italics with their n, without a rank or colour, and are not used in mismatch findings. Minimums: 4th-down decisions 10; FG attempts 8; QB designed runs 8; QB designed runs faced 8; clear go spots 5; deep attempts 15; deep attempts faced 15; end-of-half drives 5; goal-to-go trips 5; plays after a three-and-out 15; plays after a turnover 15; plays leading by 9+ 30; plays trailing by 9+ 30; scrambles 8; scrambles faced 8. Every other rate shows its sample size when you hover the cell.

Recent form, replacements, pressure, big plays and referees

  • Recent form: each play of a team's last four games is adjusted with the season's opponent effects and home coefficient (EPA minus the opponent's defensive or offensive effect and the home term); the average over all of a team's plays equals its opponent-adjusted EPA/play, so the four-game and season figures are on the same scale. Four games are about 250 plays per unit, so changes under about 0.05 EPA/play are ordinary noise.
  • Next man up: the replacement named by the depth chart, judged on his own 2026 sample (receivers and backs: targets, carries and EPA; pass rushers and linebackers: snaps and PFR pressures; linemen and defensive backs: the unit's EPA per dropback in games he started, meaning 50%+ of snaps, against the other games).
  • Quarterbacks under pressure: EPA per dropback when hit or sacked against clean dropbacks (play-by-play qb_hit and sack flags), with dropback counts, sack and scramble rates.
  • Expected starter: where a team's season figures mix quarterbacks, the matchup tables add a line for this week's expected starter: the latest game's starter (30+ dropbacks) unless he is on the reserve list or listed Out/Doubtful, otherwise the healthy quarterback with the most starts. It uses his own dropbacks (opponent-adjusted EPA, success, sack and interception-worthy rates); under four starts it is marked low confidence. The rule cannot see a trade, a signing or a coach's decision, so a small hand-kept file adds those for the coming week, each with its source (a team announcement or a named reporter): the named starter then replaces the rule, his own 2026 sample counts every team he played for, and a quarterback with no regular-season dropbacks is shown with no sample. The team rows are not changed: they still describe the quarterbacks who played.
  • Big plays allowed by position: completions of 20+ yards and yards after the catch allowed to the receiver's weekly-roster position, per target and per game.
  • Referee crews: accepted penalties per game (same rules as the team tables) in the games each referee worked in 2024-25; the referee comes from the nflverse schedules, which name him for 65 of 136 2026 games so far. This week's assignments come from a hand-kept file with its source and date (loaded).
  • Absences: snap-count players are linked to rosters through the nflverse players table (PFR id to gsis id), then the roster's own PFR id, then team and name. Each player's status is his latest weekly-roster row. A regular inactive (INA) for each of the team's last three games with no injury designation counts as out ("inactive 3+ games"); a player active on a roster dated after a missed game is not flagged; a report for a game the player then played is not counted.
  • Regulars: 50%+ of offensive or defensive snaps in the games he played, at least two games, and at least half of the team's games up to his last appearance (a starter hurt early stays in; a fill-in with two late games stays out), one row per player at his most-played position. A quarterback counts only when he started the team's latest game or has its most starts (a backup is not an absence). Each absence shows when he last played and how many team games he has missed: new = 0-1 games, long-term = 2 or more. A long-term absence states how many of the team's games the player was part of; "mostly reflected in the season numbers" is said only when his current run of missed games is at least half of them, and never for a quarterback. Only new absences go into the takeaways.
  • Injury statuses: on the Tuesday build the coming week's practice reports do not exist yet, so every status is labelled "last week's report (week N)" (teams off a bye use an older week). A status refresh after the final injury reports (Friday about 16:30 ET; Thursday for a Thursday game) re-downloads the injury reports, rosters and depth charts and rebuilds only the absences, next man up, arrivals, quarterback scenarios and the per-game files (refresh_status.py). The practice-concern column is hidden until the coming week's practice reports exist.
  • New arrivals and departures: active players whose latest roster team differs from an earlier 2026 week, or who joined in season (signing, practice-squad promotion), shown when they were regulars elsewhere (40%+ of snaps in at least two games) or play 40%+ of snaps for the new team, with their 2026 sample (sacks and QB hits from play-by-play, PFR pressures, targets and carries, or the unit's numbers in their starts). Departures are former regulars of a team now on another roster; a departure is new for one team game after his last. Moves come from the weekly rosters (through week 10), so a later trade appears after the next roster update.
  • Unusual games: a game is flagged when the play-by-play weather text shows rain, snow or 15+ mph wind (not a dome or closed roof) and combined dropbacks are under 56, the bottom 2% of 1359 2021-25 regular-season games (median 79). Season and last-four figures are shown with and without it. A quarterback who threw 2+ interceptions in his team's latest game gets FTN's interception-worthy and uncatchable counts against his earlier games; that charting cannot separate a wet ball from a bad decision. Display only: no rating or expectation changes.
  • Headline edges are scored on the matchup models' shrunk effects (each unit's effect times the share the shrinkage keeps, in standard deviations of the true effects), so a measure with no reliable signal cannot top the list. Blitz tendencies have no shrinkage model and stay as context in the matchup report.
  • Player rates are shown with their sample and only from a minimum: 10 targets or carries for EPA per target or carry, 20 dropbacks for a quarterback's EPA against the blitz or when hit, 100 dropbacks on each side of a with/without split.
  • ESPN win rates: the hand-copied file is checked on load (32 teams, four metrics, values 0-100, ranks 1-32, same through-week as the report); it failed (file runs through week 8, the report through week 9), so the columns are hidden.

Sign conventions

Defensive EPA, success and yards are what the defence allows, so lower is better (▼ in the header); every composite, rating and situational score is oriented so higher is better (▲). Ranks are always 1 = best for that unit, and the Team chart flips any lower-is-better axis so up and right are good.

Quality checks

  • EP scale: play-by-play 2021-2026 is on the original nflfastR EP valuation (two-point probability 0.4735), the scale every historical fit here uses.
  • Schedule lists 136 regular-season games in weeks 1-9; play-by-play contains 136; 136 have final scores.
  • Opponent adjustment: home-field coefficient -0.010 EPA/play for the offence (half the home/away gap); play-level residual variance 1.848.
  • Drive points reconcile with final scores in 136 of 136 games (max gap 0 pts; gaps come from scores on plays outside a scrimmage drive).
  • Drives: 2969 built, 139 excluded (kneel-only, or started with 30 s or less left in a half).
  • Recent form: last four games per team; season values from the same residual method differ from the adjusted EPA/play by at most 0.0013.
  • FTN charting: 99.3% of 2026 pass attempts charted (missing: 2026_09_BUF_MIN). League P(INT | interception-worthy) = 0.586; P(INT | not) = 0.0036. Historical own-fumble loss rate 0.486 (2021-2025).
  • FTN box counts: 6,762 charted designed rushes; 54.8% faced 7 or more in the box, 8.2% 8 or more. QB-fault sacks: 129 of 635 charted sacks.
  • Run direction: 6,578 designed runs with a location (55.4% inside). Targets by position: 99.9% of 8,534 targets went to a WR, TE or RB on the weekly roster (the rest: QBs, linemen or unmatched); 8,916 attempts with a throw zone.
  • PFR advanced passing: 244 of 272 team-games available (122 games); pressure and PFR-blitz rates use only those games.
  • PFR advanced receiving: 122 of 136 games available; receiving broken tackles and drops use only those games.
  • Absences: 756 regulars; 756 linked to a gsis id (755 through the nflverse players table); 0 with no weekly-roster match.
  • Injury reports: 144 regulars listed on a report for a game they then played are not flagged.
  • Absence classes: 52 on the reserve list, 1 inactive 3+ games, 0 unconfirmed; 50 regulars who missed a game are active on a later roster and not flagged; 20 OL regulars counted out; 21 confirmed absences are new (0-1 games missed), 66 long-term.
  • Duplicate players in absences: 0 (16 players listed at two positions were merged under their most-played position, and 0 duplicate roster ids removed; 0 remain).
  • Matchup calibration: shrinkage weights multiplied by a week-9 factor per measure (EPA/play 0.80, EPA/dropback 0.72, EPA/rush 0.62, pressure 0.47, red-zone TD rate 0.05), fitted on 2021-25 (1,916 team-games per measure); out of sample it lowered the error on 17 of 17 measures.
  • Quarterback news (hand-kept, with sources, for what rosters and injury reports cannot show yet): week 10 starters ARI Carson Beck (named), BAL Jacoby Brissett (expected), LV Fernando Mendoza (named), MIA Kyle McCord (named), MIN Kirk Cousins (expected). Injury reports still decide game statuses.
  • Referees: crew rates from 2024-25 (18 referees); nflverse schedules name the referee for 65 of 136 2026 games (weeks 1, 2, 3, 4, 5); week 10 assignments loaded for 14 games.
  • Unusual games: rain, snow or 15+ mph wind and under 56 combined dropbacks (bottom 2% of 1359 2021-25 games, median 79, lowest 40): 2 flagged this season, 9 met both tests in 2021-25. 6 quarterbacks threw 2+ interceptions in their team's latest game.
  • Weather: 7 forecasts, 4 with the roof not listed, 3 indoors, 0 already started, 0 not loaded. History from 922 outdoor games with a usable weather text.
  • Play-caller check against Sam Hoppen's play-caller dataset (read 11 Nov 2026 21:39 UTC), games through week 9: all 808 entries agree. Marked unclear in the file: WAS defence (Daronte Jones or Dan Quinn; the dataset lists Dan Quinn).
  • Next man up: 98 absences have a listed replacement; 88 matched to his own 2026 sample.
  • Arrivals: 26 active players on a new team since week 1 who were regulars elsewhere or play 40%+ of snaps (8 former regulars elsewhere, 7 arrived in weeks 8-10). Departures: 8 former regulars now on another team (2 new). Rosters through week 10.

Reproduce

.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\team_analytics\compute.py --season 2026 --through-week 9
.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\team_analytics\build_html.py --dir reports\team_analytics\2026_week10

Outputs: team_metrics.csv (every team metric), quarterbacks.csv, team_games.csv, drives.csv, penalty_types.csv, absences.csv, offensive_line.csv, bundle_meta.json. No market data is read: spread, total and price columns are dropped on load.

Data: nflverse (nflfastR play-by-play, FTN charting, PFR advanced stats, Next Gen Stats, snap counts, rosters, injuries, schedules). ESPN win rates copied by hand with their date. For analysis and education only. Generated by scripts/team_analytics in the nflcast project.
